title: Attain the exact native square and sharp tensor witness in four-axis rounding (no new κ)
body:
Construct a four-axis Gaussian-grid bijection with sharp error sqrt(8) h, exact sum, global unit covariance, integral-image exactness, F²=J and F⁴=I. This resolves the missing square in #6758 and attains #6761's real affine-period lower bound with index 4096.

The certified F(e0)=e3 also attains squared discrepancy 24 on the companion obstruction's fixed tensor witness, while retaining bounded error and the exact square. This is not a worst-case discrepancy optimum or row/column commutation.

Base: 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a.
#6758: 362b20bc934500bc503e850059f0d34daa5dcae3.
#6761: b78c8938b6d04b7c340c06d4e958947aeecd9270.
Exact file, predecessor and companion pins: SOURCES.json.
Certificate SHA256: 44a950a62abec947b4c094c2c1f290bec2f8d7f41d3a108ab4c58b5bdfc46b56.

Reproduce (Python 3.12, stdlib):
```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/four-axis-exact-square-grid
```
Expected: `PASS_FOUR_AXIS_EXACT_SQUARE_GRID`, `PASS_INDEPENDENT_SHARP_TENSOR_COMPOSITION`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

Executed: all 4096 real classes, 4096 complex fixtures, inverse compositions, eight large-word fixtures through 4091 bits and nine rejection controls, including a locally valid but square-incompatible orbit. Separate dense-Walsh/lattice reviews and descending-section reconstruction check all 256 tensor entries. All eight normal/-O commands, metadata, committed bytes/modes and Git-free checks pass. Fixed-period discovery forced the basis cycle, tried seed 0 and stopped on a complete matching; it regenerates the certificate byte for byte. No exhaustive rounder search.

No new κ. The raw block uses 160 word additions and 32 quarter divisions; classifier, lookup, routing, precision and reversible cleanup still need a complete paid caller implementation. All five selected assumptions remain.

By @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and separate mathematical/algorithmic review. Credit Nick Petalas (#6574), #6758/#6761, ToikY (#6755) and Ali Romman (#6509). No human/proof-kernel acceptance.

Proof, certificate, reviews and limits: https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/tree/6ea7d0886e62d6c0f53aa90ae8691dbcc61ea04a/research/four-axis-exact-square-grid
